title: They Said Memes Were Harmless — We Found the Ones That Hurt: Decoding Jokes, Symbols, and Cultural References

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating abuse detection models on the MAMI (Multimodal Misogyny) dataset to classify explicit and implicit misogynistic content, sexism, stereotypes, and objectification in memes.
Evaluating models on the FHM (Hateful Memes) and Harm-C/P datasets to detect racist caricatures, racial slurs, and exclusionary anti-immigrant narratives embedded in multimodal memes.
Assessing the detection of harmful propaganda, exclusionary discourse, and extremist ideologies (e.g., alt-right symbols, swastikas) using the Harm-C/P benchmark and culturally-grounded reasoning.

Measuring classification performance (Macro-F1 and Accuracy) on the GOAT-Bench overarching categories (Harmfulness, Hatefulness, Offensiveness) to detect broad offensive language, toxic satire, and multimodal hate speech.
